title: Georgia's 9th Congressional District general election, 2026
description: The general election for Georgia's 9th Congressional District pits two-term Republican incumbent Andrew Clyde against Democratic nominee Caitlyn Gegen. The district covers a largely rural and exurban swath northeast of Atlanta, including Gainesville, Dahlonega, and Toccoa. Cook Political Report rated the seat as Solidly Republican ahead of the May 19 primary, making Clyde the heavy favorite. The race highlights contrasting visions on economic policy, healthcare, and the role of government, with Clyde emphasizing conservative fiscal and social values and Gegen advocating for universal healthcare, raising the minimum wage, and protecting reproductive rights.
polling_note: No general-election head-to-head polls were found for this race. The Cook Political Report rated the district as Solidly Republican prior to the primary. The last competitive polling in the district was during the 2020 primary cycle.

candidates.name: Andrew Clyde
candidates.summary: Andrew Clyde is a U.S. Navy combat veteran and small business owner who has represented Georgia's 9th Congressional District since January 2021. He owns Clyde Armory, a firearms business he founded in 1991, and serves on the House Appropriations and Budget Committees. Clyde is a staunch conservative known for his opposition to IRS civil asset forfeiture, his support for the Second Amendment, and his America First policy positions.

candidates.name: Caitlyn Gegen
candidates.summary: Caitlyn Gegen is a community organizer and University of Georgia alumna (BA in International Relations, MPA) who also holds an MSc from the London School of Economics. She defeated Nick Alex in the May 19 Democratic primary to become the party's nominee in Georgia's 9th District. Her campaign focuses on protecting reproductive rights, advocating for universal healthcare, raising the federal minimum wage to $15 per hour, investing in clean energy, and breaking up corporate monopolies.

forecast.rationale: GA-09 is a heavily Republican district (rural and exurban northeast Georgia). Two-term incumbent Andrew Clyde (R) is the heavy favorite against Democratic nominee Caitlyn Gegen. Cook Political Report rated the seat Solidly Republican ahead of the primary. No general-election head-to-head polls exist, so the forecast relies on structural indicators: strong Republican partisanship of the district, incumbency advantage, and the absence of any signals suggesting competitiveness. Confidence is medium rather than high due to zero current polling, but the available race context overwhelmingly favors Clyde.
